Product directions

Panels, portable formats, LED masks and flexible mat/bag platforms. Match the exact version and contents to the quoted SKU rather than a broad catalogue label.

Explore cooperation paths →

Qualification and supply

Plan quality verification →

MAKE TRUST REVIEWABLE

Ask for evidence that supports the decision.

Factory photographs, company descriptions and platform pages introduce a sourcing discussion. They do not replace a buyer audit, an exact-model report or a signed commercial offer. Request the company, product and production records appropriate to the proposed scope.

We do not use this page to claim undisclosed OEM customer relationships, a blanket medical approval or independently verified superiority over another supplier. Named client references need supporting cooperation records and permission to display them.

Eine klare Spezifikation ist der Anfang.

APTREDLIGHT / FAQ

Antworten für Ihren Einkauf.

Die wichtigsten Punkte vor Ihrer ersten Musterbestellung.

Kann ich meine eigene Marke verwenden?

Logo, Produktkennzeichnung, Anleitung und Verpackung können für die gewählte Plattform besprochen werden. Umfang und Mindestbestellmenge sind schriftlich zu bestätigen.

Wie hoch ist die Mindestbestellmenge?

Sie hängt von Modell und Anpassungsumfang ab. Bitten Sie um ein Angebot mit getrennten Kosten für Muster, Werkzeuge, Verpackung und Versand.

Welche Prüfunterlagen sollte ich anfordern?

Fordern Sie Spezifikation, Bedienungsanleitung, elektrische Daten und verfügbare Prüfberichte für das genaue Modell und den Zielmarkt an.

Wie wird die Anfrage versendet?

Das Formular erstellt eine Nachricht. Erst wenn Sie sie selbst in WhatsApp oder Alibaba absenden, wird Ihre Anfrage übermittelt.

APTREDLIGHT / FAQ

Les réponses utiles à vos achats.

Les points essentiels avant votre première commande d’échantillons.

Puis-je utiliser ma propre marque ?

Le logo, l’étiquetage, la notice et l’emballage peuvent être étudiés pour la plateforme choisie. Le périmètre et la quantité minimale doivent être confirmés par écrit.

Quelle est la quantité minimale ?

Elle dépend du modèle et des adaptations. Demandez un devis détaillant les échantillons, l’outillage, l’emballage et le transport.

Quels documents demander ?

Demandez la fiche technique, la notice, les caractéristiques électriques et les rapports disponibles pour le modèle exact et le marché visé.

Comment envoyer ma demande ?

Le formulaire prépare un message. La demande est transmise uniquement lorsque vous l’envoyez vous-même sur WhatsApp ou Alibaba.

APTREDLIGHT / OEM & ODM BUYER GUIDE

Choose a manufacturer
with a clearer buying framework.

A practical guide to specification, evidence and approval for brand owners, distributors and sourcing managers. Start with the intended product and market, then compare what each offer actually includes.

APTREDLIGHT is a Shenzhen-based OEM/ODM manufacturer of red light therapy panels, masks and flexible product platforms. We support brand-led product briefs, sample verification and model-specific sourcing discussions for projects in the US, UK, Europe and Australia.

1. Define the product and business objective.

List the product format, target customer, intended use, destination market, estimated quantity and launch priorities. Separate mandatory requirements from preferred features. An entry panel, a flexible bag and a voice-control mask need different development and acceptance questions.

Use current platform references such as T300 panels, A13 portable panels, Smart AI Voice Red Light Therapy Mask, Red Light Wellness Mat or the 3050 ULTRA flexible blanket/bag platform. A product direction is not a signed specification or proof that every requested variant is released.

2. Agree the cooperation and ownership boundary.

Distinguish branding an existing platform, changing a configuration and developing an original product. Ask the supplier to identify available options, engineering review, validation and commercial scope for each request. Resolve design, tooling, firmware, artwork, confidentiality and change-control responsibilities in writing.

For a second-source evaluation, identify which requirements must match and which may differ. Share only the material your brand owns or has permission to disclose. Do not assume that reproducing a similar appearance is technically or legally sufficient.

3. Compare measurable optical requirements.

Request wavelength allocation and a measured spectrum for the selected configuration. Compare irradiance only with the unit, instrument, measurement distance, operating mode, sampling grid and coverage stated. Separate a center reading from an average over a defined area.

Keep electrical input power, nominal LED ratings and optical quantities separately labeled. A figure in W is not automatically irradiance at a working distance, and a wavelength list is not a treatment or penetration-depth promise.

4. Match documents to the model, use and market.

Ask for the configuration sheet, relevant test reports or declarations, labeling and instructions for the exact quoted SKU. Check issuer, document number, model identifiers, scope and dates. Company-level records and component documents do not automatically establish finished-product authorization.

Define the intended claims and destination requirements before artwork approval. The US, UK, Europe and Australia are sourcing markets in this guide, not blanket regulatory approvals. Where classification or market obligations are uncertain, obtain qualified professional advice.

Prepare a model-specific document request → · Review public document scopes →

5. Compare the complete commercial offer.

Use the same product configuration, quantities, accessories, packaging, validation and delivery assumptions when comparing quotations. Record what is included and what remains open; an omitted cost is not evidence that an offer is cheaper.

Decision areaEvidence or terms to requestOpen item to resolve
ConfigurationModel, revision, controls, accessories, dimensions and packagingWhich exact build does the price cover?
PerformanceSpectrum, irradiance method, test plane, operating mode and coverageAre the measurement conditions comparable?
DevelopmentFeasibility, samples, tooling, ownership and approval milestonesWhich changes need engineering or additional validation?
QualitySample criteria, inspection plan, traceability and deviation processWhat evidence demonstrates acceptance?
Delivery and supportNamed terms/place, packing, freight scope, warranty and defect handlingWho owns each responsibility after shipment?

6. Define the sample decision before ordering it.

Agree which checks the sample must pass and which documents must be reviewed. Include configuration, dimensions, controls, usability, instructions, labels, optical conditions, accessories and packing. Record deviations and restrictions; receiving a sample is not complete supplier qualification.

Retain an identified reference sample with the approved configuration revision. Review the five-step project verification framework to agree the checks and records appropriate to your order.

7. Preserve the decision for repeat supply.

Reference the approved configuration on repeat orders. Agree notification and review rules for relevant components, materials, firmware, labels and packing changes. Keep inspection outcomes and issue closure records associated with the actual order rather than an unversioned brochure.

Prepare the next useful deliverable.

A first discussion should lead to an agreed configuration proposal, feasibility review, evidence request or sample plan. Write down the next owner, deliverable and decision gate. Request model-specific terms instead of assuming universal MOQ, lead time, output, certification or warranty promises.

What to verify before your first red light therapy OEM sample

A useful sample order begins with an agreed specification. Give every supplier the same brief so your comparison leads to a clear purchasing decision.

1. Identify the exact version

Record the model name, wavelength list, LED layout, controller version, accessories and packaging. Ask whether your sample matches the version proposed for bulk production. A shared product name alone does not define a configuration.

2. Make output measurements comparable

Request the measurement distance, meter model, operating mode, measurement positions and test conditions alongside irradiance results. Keep electrical input power, nominal LED ratings and measured optical output in separate fields. Figures collected under different conditions should not be treated as equivalent.

3. Evaluate the experience and documentation

Review controls, mounting, packaging, labels and the instructions supplied with the sample. Request documents that identify the exact model and configuration. Record any unavailable evidence as an open item before your purchasing decision.

4. Put commercial terms in writing

Confirm sample charges, customization scope, minimum quantities, lead time, delivery terms and warranty responsibilities. Agree how specification changes will be approved and how the production order will be inspected.

Red Light Therapy OEM Repeat Orders: A Buyer’s Guide to Change Control

An approved sample is a reference point. A repeat order needs a clear record of what stays the same, what changes and who approves the difference.

For brands buying red light therapy panels, mats or wraps for the US, UK, Europe and Australia, a repeat purchase can involve a new destination, revised packaging or a different controller. Treat each change as an explicit decision before production. This guide outlines a practical purchasing workflow to discuss with APTREDLIGHT; it does not claim that every product already has the same documentation package.

1. Create an approved configuration record

Give the accepted configuration a revision number and approval date. Keep the physical sample identifier, written specification and artwork files together. A phrase such as “same as last time” leaves room for different interpretations when a team member, destination or component changes.

RecordWhat to identifyWhat the buyer checks
Product and light configurationExact model, version, agreed wavelength layout and operating modes.The repeat-order specification refers to the approved version.
Controls and powerController or firmware revision where applicable, input specification and supplied plug or adapter.Any proposed substitution is listed before production.
Mechanical parts and accessoriesHousing finish, mounting parts, stand, cables and included items.Fit, included quantities and assembly instructions match the order.
Brand materialsLabel, manual, carton and insert file revisions.Approved languages, model references and artwork are consistent.
Acceptance evidenceAgreed inspection criteria, measurement conditions and report references.Records identify the configuration and batch being reviewed.

2. Ask for a change proposal before accepting a substitution

If a component or packaging material becomes unavailable, request the current item, proposed replacement, reason for the change and affected orders. Ask what evaluation is needed and whether previously supplied documents still cover the revised configuration. Do not assume that a visually similar part is interchangeable.

For an optical configuration change, request comparable measurement conditions. For a controller change, agree which functions will be checked. For packaging changes, review product protection, included accessories and the updated packing arrangement. These are purchasing review points, not a universal test protocol.

3. Use a short approval sequence

  1. Describe: document the proposed change and the baseline revision.
  2. Review: identify affected functions, instructions, packaging and supporting evidence.
  3. Verify: agree any revised sample, targeted evaluation or document review needed.
  4. Approve: record the buyer’s decision, date and new revision.
  5. Identify: specify the first order or batch using the approved change.

Keep pending changes separate from released specifications. If approval is incomplete, explicitly agree how the affected production will be handled rather than allowing assumptions to become order instructions.

4. Separate destination versions

A brand selling into several countries may need different plugs, packaging languages, instructions or labeling arrangements. Define destination variants under separate SKU or revision references. Confirm the exact configuration and available documentation for each market with the responsible parties before release; a successful order for one destination does not establish suitability for every destination.

5. Close the loop at shipment and receiving

Request a shipment record linking the purchase order, product revision, batch identifier, packed quantity and agreed inspection documents. On receipt, compare a selected unit and its accessories, labels and packaging with that record. Report discrepancies with clear photographs and identifiers so both teams discuss the same unit and revision.

For replacement accessories or after-sales parts, include the affected product revision. Ask the supplier to confirm compatibility rather than relying only on the model name.

We plan to reorder [model] against approved specification [revision/date] and previous order [reference], for [destination]. How to qualify a red light therapy second-source manufacturer

Published 17 November 2026 · APTREDLIGHT sourcing desk

An established wellness brand may evaluate a second red light therapy manufacturer to reduce dependence on one supply route, introduce a differentiated product or create a more resilient launch plan. A second source becomes useful when it can reproduce the requirements your brand actually needs. A similar housing, wavelength label or headline price is not enough.

This guide describes a qualification process for brand founders, sourcing managers and product teams. It is a planning framework, not a promise that every factory or product already meets the requirements below.

Existing APTREDLIGHT company photograph used to illustrate a manufacturing discussion. It is not evidence of a particular customer's project, a factory audit result or exact-model performance testing.

1. Define why your brand needs a second source

Start with one business objective. Is the priority continuity of supply, a distinct feature set, a different product format or support for a new market? Assign a project owner and state what the evaluation must demonstrate. Keep the existing supply commitments separate from the qualification schedule.

Record the required product format, destination market, intended use, expected ordering pattern and acceptable differences from your current offer. Do not ask a new supplier to copy another party's protected design. Identify which drawings, tooling, firmware, artwork and specifications your brand owns or has permission to share.

2. Write a transfer boundary before requesting a sample

A red light therapy second-source manufacturer needs an explicit supply boundary. Distinguish the requirements that must match from features that can change. Physical appearance, user controls, packaging and servicing arrangements may each have different constraints.

Prepare a short requirements matrix with three columns: mandatory, preferred and open for proposal. For a panel, include dimensions, mounting interface, electrical input, controls and accessories. Define optical requirements using the measurement conditions your team will accept. For a flexible product, add materials, seams, cleaning instructions, controller connections and packing requirements.

Ask the supplier to identify feasibility gaps and required development work in writing. An unresolved item should remain a gap rather than silently becoming an assumed capability.

3. Compare equivalent evidence, not equivalent brochures

Request documentation for the exact configuration being quoted. Check the model identifier, revision and test conditions. Irradiance figures taken at different distances or using different methods cannot establish that two products are interchangeable.

Separate supplier-level credentials from model-specific reports. Likewise, a component document does not automatically cover the complete finished product. Confirm the documentation applicable to the intended use and destination market with qualified advice where necessary.

Use the same checklist for both sources. Missing information should be visible in the comparison, with an owner and a next step. Avoid ranking suppliers by the number of certificates, LED count or nominal wattage alone.

4. Agree the pilot acceptance criteria in advance

A pilot order should test the risks that matter before a broader transition. Agree which reference sample controls production, which configuration revision is approved and what inspection records are required. Include usability, labeling, packaging and accessory checks alongside optical and electrical requirements.

Define the handling of deviations before placing the order. Which changes require approval? Who reviews a nonconforming unit? What evidence closes an issue? Record these decisions in the purchase specification rather than relying on a message thread alone.

Do not move the complete range at once simply because one sample looks promising. A staged evaluation makes it easier to distinguish a product issue from a packaging, instruction or delivery issue.

5. Evaluate continuity and total supply scope

Compare quotations using the same configuration, quantity assumptions, accessories, testing, packaging and delivery terms. Include development, tooling, sample and logistics costs where applicable. Ask how warranty support, spare parts and configuration changes will be handled after shipment.

A lower unit price can be valuable, but only when the offer covers the scope your brand requires. Do not turn an incomplete quote into a complete cost comparison. Keep commercial assumptions explicit and request a revised offer when the scope changes.

6. Make the approval decision traceable

Finish the evaluation with a brief decision record: accepted requirements, remaining restrictions, approved sample reference, document versions and conditions for the next order. Retain the reasons for approval, conditional approval or rejection. A repeat order should reference that record and require review when the supplier proposes a material change.

This notice explains how APTREDLIGHT uses the information you provide through connected website enquiry forms. It covers responding to product and OEM/ODM requests; submitting a form does not subscribe you to marketing or place an order.

Notice updated: 16 November 2026.

What happens when you press “Send enquiry”?

Your enquiry is sent to our website service and stored in private enquiry records for our team to review. We show delivery success only after the service confirms receipt. WhatsApp and Alibaba remain separate, optional contact channels.

Do not include sensitive personal information, confidential customer data, passwords, payment details or technical drawings in the public form. It does not accept file attachments. Arrange a suitable secure exchange with our team when your project needs one.

2. Contact permission and use

The required enquiry checkbox asks for permission to store the request and contact you to respond. It does not authorize automatic newsletter enrollment, advertising campaigns or automatic messages through WhatsApp. We may use your details to clarify requirements, discuss samples and quotations, and maintain the related business conversation.

Enquiry records are intended for authorized personnel managing the request. They are not exposed through a public enquiry list. We use hosting and storage infrastructure to operate the website and private enquiry records.

3. Attribution and browser storage

The enquiry script keeps bounded first-touch and current campaign labels in browser session storage when available, with an in-memory fallback. It does not store your contact fields or message in session storage or local storage. The fields remain in the open form when delivery fails so that you can review or retry them. Closing or reloading the page may lose unsubmitted content.

Campaign labels can be incomplete, altered by a link, or unavailable. We do not treat them as verified customer identity. We avoid retaining contact-looking values in these labels and do not include enquiry contents, request IDs or UTM values in our confirmed-enquiry analytics event.

4. Analytics choices

Our website uses Google measurement tools to understand page visits and intentional actions. A website enquiry is different from a WhatsApp click, an enquiry confirmed by the server, a sales-qualified opportunity or an order. We do not describe a click as a completed sale.

The enquiry script’s confirmed-receipt event is suppressed when the browser signals Global Privacy Control, the site sets analytics consent to false, or an existing website analytics opt-out is active. The form can still be submitted for a response. This notice does not assert that every analytics tag or third-party service supports every browser preference. Use any available site consent controls and your browser’s privacy settings for broader choices.

Google Analytics may use cookies and process device and visit information according to its configuration. For provider details, see Google’s privacy policy. Do not share contact details in public URLs or campaign tags.

Own-site AI discovery counters

When an observed website source indicates ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude or Copilot, an additional own-site service can count a landing-page view, the start of an enquiry form and an intentional WhatsApp-link click. It sends a fixed page category, normalized first/current AI source and medium, allowlisted campaign/content identifiers, an allowed AI referring hostname, controlled landing paths, a random event reference and a technical-test flag. It does not send your name, email, phone, enquiry message, lead receipt ID, AI conversation or prompt, full URL, arbitrary UTM text or search terms. An optional buyer-declared discovery source is saved with your enquiry separately and is not used to manufacture historical page visits.

These counters do not verify unique people, advertising impressions, spend or completed messages. A ChatGPT referring hostname does not establish whether a visit came from paid advertising or an organic answer; a paid UTM tag is an unverified source label, not proof that an advertisement ran. Browser privacy and missing referrers can make coverage incomplete.

The counters are not sent when our analytics consent flag is false, Global Privacy Control is enabled or the existing site analytics opt-out is active. Session storage, with a page-memory fallback when blocked, limits duplicate view/form-start events; these transport references are not linked to your lead receipt or added to GA event parameters. Intentional WhatsApp clicks remain separate from messages and server-received enquiries.

5. Optional WhatsApp and Alibaba contact

We do not automatically send your form to WhatsApp or Alibaba. A manual WhatsApp fallback may open a link containing the enquiry details you choose to send; WhatsApp receives the link information when you open it, and you must press Send to deliver the message. Copying details only places them on your device clipboard; you choose where to paste them.

Alibaba links open our official storefront. Their services, sign-in, orders and privacy handling operate separately under the respective provider’s terms. Review WhatsApp’s privacy policy and the privacy information available through our Alibaba storefront before using those channels.

6. Retention and requests

We retain enquiry information for the time needed to respond and manage the related business discussion, subject to any applicable recordkeeping obligations. We have not committed to a fixed automatic deletion interval on this page. Internal archive status does not by itself mean that data has been deleted.

To ask about access, correction or deletion of an enquiry, contact the APTREDLIGHT team through our existing official WhatsApp contact. Include enough context to identify your enquiry, such as its date and company name; do not send passwords or unnecessary identity documents. We may need to verify the request before acting and will explain relevant limitations.

7. Scope and updates

This is a practical website notice, not a claim of legal certification, medical-device approval or universal compliance with every jurisdiction. How a particular business request must be handled depends on its context and applicable requirements. We may update the notice as the enquiry service changes.

Quality decisions need
an agreed evidence trail.

Use this five-step project verification framework to define the checks, acceptance criteria and records for the exact configuration you plan to order. It is a proposed buyer-supplier workflow, not proof that every test is completed for every model.

These stages are evidence requests and agreement points. Confirm availability and actual execution records for your project; this framework does not claim an independently certified factory SOP or blanket product approval.

01

Incoming components and configuration

Agree the configuration revision, relevant parts, supply scope and traceability needs. Identify the LED arrangement, power supply, controller, materials and accessories that must match the accepted design.

Evidence to agree and request

Approved configuration, component identifiers where applicable, incoming acceptance requirements and change notification responsibilities.

02

Engineering sample and optical review

Check the actual sample against agreed dimensions, controls, usability and documented optical conditions. State the instrument, measurement plane, distance, operating mode and coverage. Do not equate a photograph or a center reading with complete sample approval.

Evidence to agree and request

Identified reference sample, test conditions, documented results, deviations and signed or otherwise recorded approval.

03

In-process checkpoints

Define the assembly, workmanship and functional checkpoints appropriate to the product and order. Agree defect definitions, inspection methods and responsibility for resolving deviations. There is no universal acceptance threshold supplied by this page.

Evidence to agree and request

Project inspection plan, relevant work checkpoints, defect/deviation records and agreed escalation.

04

Final model and documentation review

Match the finished configuration, labels, instructions, accessories and applicable reports to the order. Review any safety or reliability evaluation needed for the intended use and destination. Do not treat a component certificate as finished-device approval.

Evidence to agree and request

Final inspection scope, model/revision identifiers, document list, label/manual versions and open-item decisions.

05

Packing, shipment and repeat-order traceability

Agree packing, quantities, handling, identification, shipping responsibilities and after-sales arrangements. Preserve the approved configuration for repeat orders and define which changes require buyer review.

Evidence to agree and request

Packing checks, order/batch identification, delivery assumptions, issue-handling terms and repeat-order revision control.

Keep unresolved items visible.

Use a project record to identify the requirement, available evidence, reviewer, outcome and next action. If a report or test does not exist for the exact model, record the gap and the proposed validation instead of describing it as complete.

Separate agreed acceptance from market authorization. A well-documented sample decision does not, on its own, establish permission for a claim or sale in every destination.

Ask for irradiance in mW/cm² with the measurement distance, instrument, operating mode, positions and test conditions. Separate electrical input power from LED nominal ratings and measured optical output. For temperature, noise, flicker or EMF figures, ask for the measurement method and conditions.

3. Model-specific supporting documents

Share your destination market and intended product use. Request available reports and declarations with matching model identifiers, versions and scope. Resolve any gaps before approving the order or making claims on your own product listing.

4. Production and acceptance plan

Agree on the approved sample, configuration change control, inspection criteria, aging-test scope, traceability, packaging checks and pre-shipment review. Put the agreed requirements into the purchase specification.

5. Written commercial terms

Confirm sample and bulk pricing, minimum quantities, development fees, lead time, included accessories, delivery terms, warranty coverage and responsibility for after-sales handling.
